outline.chapter_title: Motivation and Overview: From RLHF Complexity to Direct Preference Optimization
outline.description: Introduce the alignment problem for large language models, why steerability is needed, the standard RLHF pipeline and its drawbacks, and how DPO provides a simpler alternative that optimizes the same objective without RL.
subtopics: Why unsupervised pretraining is not enough for controllability
Relative preferences vs demonstrations: data efficiency and practicality
The RLHF pipeline at a glance and its pain points (instability, complexity, compute)
Core idea of DPO: map preferences to policy learning with a simple classification loss
Contributions of the paper and empirical highlights

outline.chapter_title: Background: Language Models, Instruction Tuning, and Preference Data
outline.description: Review foundational concepts needed to understand DPO, including LMs, instruction tuning, and the mechanics of collecting and representing human preference data.
subtopics: Autoregressive language models and conditional generation
Instruction tuning vs few-shot prompting
Preference data formats: pairwise comparisons and rankings
Sources of preference data: human raters and AI feedback (RLAIF)
Notation for prompts, completions, and datasets

outline.chapter_title: RLHF Pipeline: SFT, Reward Modeling, and PPO Fine-Tuning
outline.description: Explain the standard RLHF approach in detail, including supervised fine-tuning, fitting a reward model from preferences, and RL optimization under a KL constraint.
subtopics: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) to obtain a reference policy
Reward modeling from preferences with logistic/BCE loss
KL-regularized RL objective for policy optimization
Using PPO/REINFORCE in practice and challenges
Why KL constraints prevent mode collapse and distribution drift

outline.description: Develop the probabilistic models used to connect latent rewards to observed preferences, focusing on Bradley–Terry for pairwise and Plackett–Luce for lists.
subtopics: Bradley–Terry model for pairwise preferences
Plackett–Luce model for ranked lists
Binary cross-entropy likelihood for reward modeling
Identifiability and under-specification in preference models
Implications for learning: only reward differences matter

outline.chapter_title: KL-Regularized Reward Maximization and the Optimal Policy Form
outline.description: Present the KL-constrained objective common in RLHF and derive the corresponding closed-form optimal policy, highlighting the role of the reference policy and the partition function.
subtopics: Objective: maximize expected reward minus beta times KL to reference
Deriving the optimal policy: exponentiated reward times reference
Partition function (normalizer) and its intractability
Relationship to control-as-inference and entropy-regularized RL
Why closed-form is useful but hard to compute directly

outline.chapter_title: From Rewards to Policies: The DPO Change-of-Variables Derivation
outline.description: Show how DPO reparameterizes the reward in terms of policy log-odds against the reference so that preference likelihood can be expressed directly as a function of the policy.
subtopics: Rewriting reward as beta times log(policy/reference) plus a prompt-dependent constant
How partition functions cancel in Bradley–Terry differences
DPO policy likelihood: preference probability in terms of policy log-odds
The DPO loss: a binary cross-entropy over preference pairs
Equivalence to optimizing the same RLHF objective without explicit RL

outline.chapter_title: Inside the DPO Update: Implicit Rewards and Gradient Mechanics
outline.description: Build intuition for how DPO changes the model, how its implicit reward arises from the policy, and why dynamic weighting avoids degeneracy.
subtopics: Implicit reward r_hat = beta * log(policy/reference)
Gradient structure: increase preferred, decrease dispreferred
Importance weighting via sigmoid of reward difference
Role of beta as strength of KL regularization
Why naive unlikelihood can degenerate and how DPO avoids it

outline.description: Provide a step-by-step recipe for training with DPO, including data handling, reference model selection, computing log-probabilities, and robust training practices.
subtopics: Data preparation: pairwise preferences and sequence scoring
Choosing and initializing the reference policy
Computing per-sequence log-probabilities and handling padding/masks
Batching, sequence lengths, and numerical stability
Optimizers, learning rates, beta selection, and early stopping
Training without on-policy sampling and minimal hyperparameter tuning
Using public preference datasets sampled from unknown references

outline.chapter_title: Theoretical Foundations: Equivalence Classes and Representability
outline.description: Develop the theory behind the DPO reparameterization, clarifying reward equivalence classes, identifiability under preference models, and the representational completeness of DPO.
subtopics: Equivalence relation: rewards differing by prompt-only functions
Same preference distribution within an equivalence class
Same optimal policy within an equivalence class under KL-regularized RL
Representation theorem: any compatible reward class can be expressed as beta * log(policy/reference)
Interpretation: selecting a canonical representative where the policy is normalized

outline.description: Analyze why actor–critic (e.g., PPO) can be unstable in RLHF, how value baselines and reward normalization interact, and why DPO’s formulation circumvents these issues.
subtopics: Control-as-inference view of PPO-style objectives
High-variance gradients and the role of baselines/values
Reward normalization strategies and their fragility
How DPO’s implicit reward avoids baseline estimation
Compute, sampling, and hyperparameter simplicity of DPO

outline.chapter_title: Experimental Setup: Tasks, Models, and Baselines
outline.description: Detail the experimental design used to evaluate DPO, including datasets, model sizes, baselines, and evaluation metrics.
subtopics: Controlled sentiment generation on IMDb with classifier-based preferences
Reddit TL;DR summarization with human preferences
Anthropic Helpful–Harmless single-turn dialogue
Models: GPT-2-large, GPT-J, Pythia (2.8B/6B)
Baselines: SFT, Preferred-FT, Unlikelihood, PPO/PPO-GT, Best-of-N, prompt-only
Evaluation: reward–KL frontier, GPT-4 win rates, temperature sweeps

outline.chapter_title: Results and Analysis: Reward–KL Frontier, Summarization, Dialogue, and OOD
outline.description: Present and interpret the empirical findings, showing DPO’s superior reward–KL tradeoff, performance on summarization and dialogue, and generalization to new domains.
subtopics: Sentiment: DPO dominates PPO and even PPO with ground-truth rewards
Summarization: higher win rates, robustness across temperatures
Dialogue: quick convergence and competitive with Best-of-128
Out-of-distribution to CNN/DailyMail: DPO retains advantages
Ablations: beta effects and the cost of removing importance weighting

outline.chapter_title: Evaluation Methodology: LLM-as-Judge and Human Agreement
outline.description: Discuss the use of GPT-4 for automatic evaluation, how prompts affect judgments, and validation against human raters.
subtopics: Designing GPT-4 prompts for summarization evaluation (simple vs concise)
Correlations between GPT-4 and human judgments
Inter-annotator agreement and reliability
Prompt sensitivity and best practices
When and how to include human evaluation

outline.description: Provide actionable guidance for practitioners to obtain strong DPO performance and avoid common pitfalls.
subtopics: Choosing beta and monitoring effective KL
Learning rate, batch size, and sequence length choices
Reference model selection or approximation when SFT is missing
Preventing length bias and repetition
Checkpoint selection and temperature calibration at inference
Diagnosing degeneracy and fixing data or loss issues

outline.description: Explore how to adapt DPO beyond the basic pairwise setting and integrate it into broader alignment pipelines and modalities.
subtopics: Generalization to Plackett–Luce for multiway rankings
Multi-attribute or constrained DPO (safety, helpfulness, style)
Self-training and curriculum strategies using DPO
Combining DPO with SFT, instruction tuning, and reranking
Applying DPO ideas to other modalities (vision, speech, code)

outline.description: Critically assess the constraints of DPO and outline open research directions, including generalization, reward hacking, and scalable evaluation.
subtopics: Dependence on data representativeness and annotation quality
Reward over-optimization and signs in DPO training curves
Generalization under distribution shift and unlabeled prompts
Ethical considerations: bias, safety, and human labor
Scaling DPO to larger models and richer evaluation

outline.description: Offer practical assignments to solidify understanding, ranging from derivations to full experimental replications and extensions.
subtopics: Derive the DPO loss from the KL-regularized objective and BT model
Implement DPO for pairwise preferences on a toy LM
Reproduce the sentiment reward–KL frontier and ablate beta
Run summarization with DPO and compare GPT-4 and human judgments
Extend DPO to multiway PL preferences or multi-attribute alignment
Project: apply DPO to toxicity reduction or style control with public data
